html:
The Sicangu, or Brulé, are one of the seven Lakota nations, the Lakota people of the northern Great Plains. The name means "burnt thighs". The map puts them in the Nebraska sandhills, south of their later homes in South Dakota.

Like the other Lakota they moved onto the plains in the 1700s and became mounted bison hunters after horses reached the plains. In 1854 a quarrel over a cow led to the Grattan fight near Fort Laramie, and in 1855 the US Army attacked a Brulé camp at Blue Water Creek in revenge. Their best known leader, Spotted Tail, chose to negotiate with the United States. The bison slaughter of the 1870s ended their way of life. Today most Sicangu belong to the Rosebud and Lower Brule tribes in South Dakota. Their kin include the Oglala and Hunkpapa.
